A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AutoPresent and SlidesBench. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F support reliable comparison; relocated and renumbered material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original slide-generation experiments, human preference evaluations, and refinement results in Section 5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds code-model comparisons, further refinement rounds, and analyses of dataset composition and tool usage.

M1.justification: The NL-to-code pipeline, SlidesLib functions, LoRA-trained Llama-3.1-8B model, and refinement prompt remain unchanged. Additional refinement rounds test repeated application of the existing procedure rather than introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use SlidesBench's 310 slide decks across ten domains, approximately 7k training examples, 585 testing examples, and the same three instruction scenarios. New domain statistics characterize existing coverage rather than add datasets or tasks.

E2.justification: v2 extends the existing comparator suite with CodeLLaMA and DeepseekCoder. CodeLLaMA is evaluated with and without SlidesLib for detailed instructions with images and high-level instructions; DeepseekCoder appears for detailed-only and high-level instructions (Tables 3–4). Existing comparators remain, while CodeLLaMA's detailed-only cells are unreported.

E3.justification: Table 6 extends evaluation from zero and one refinement round to include two and three rounds, adding test-time iteration budgets. The data splits, metrics, three-candidate execution-selection procedure, human-study settings, and training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds an iteration-count ablation examining whether further refinement helps (Section 5.5, Table 6). Appendix B.3 analyzes function usage by model and instruction scenario, while Appendix A.3 adds domain-wise image and text-block statistics. Existing library comparisons and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same ICC validation, human-study response counts, paired t-tests in Table 5, and seed information in Table 7. The added experiments introduce no new repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Existing matched scores are unchanged. New results include CodeLLaMA's overall scores of 3.1 without SlidesLib and 30.3 with it in Table 3, plus additional refinement results in Table 6. Three-round scores are 60.1, 59.4, and 61.4 for detailed-with-images, detailed-only, and high-level instructions. Domain statistics and API usage percentages are also newly reported.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains the same metric definitions and mathematical expressions, including positional similarity. Neither version introduces additional formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: SlidesBench, programmatic slide generation with SlidesLib, an 8B AutoPresent model approaching GPT-4o, and benefits from refinement. Added experiments support these existing claims without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 5.5 replaces emphasis on the first-round 3.2-point detailed-only gain with the interpretation that continued refinement often helps, but the first iteration usually provides the largest improvement. The applicability boundaries and limitations in Section 7 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 newly identifies the comparator variants DeepseekCoder-7B-v1.5 and CodeLLaMA-7B-Instruct. Training parameters, library documentation, program examples, refinement prompts, and code/data access information were already provided in v1 and are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to the DeepSeek-Coder and Code Llama papers, corresponding to the new comparators. The related-work discussion and positioning against visual programming and existing slide-generation or editing approaches remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits are localized to baseline descriptions, the refinement discussion, terminology such as the 'Effect of SlidesLib' heading, and short new Appendix A.3 and B.3 subsections. The main section sequence and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 3–4 gain comparator rows, and Table 6 becomes a four-row iteration table. v2 adds domain-statistics plots in Figure 6 and a tool-usage chart in Figure 10. Existing appendix figures, prompts, and tables are retained with some relocation and renumbering; the overall layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's smaller comparator set and one-round refinement test, v2 adds relevant code-specialized baselines and tests whether refinement benefits persist (Tables 3–4 and 6). The domain and tool-usage analyses provide useful transparency. These additions modestly strengthen the empirical account, although new-baseline coverage is uneven and the core findings and limitations remain unchanged.
